operators.description:
Accumulates a value with the incoming rate.

Note that the increment is a rate that gets multiplied with the current frame duration: With an increment of 1 you have a full value change of 1 unit after one second.

Similar to [Time].
For a variant that does not count up linearly / smooth but in steps, see [Counter]

inputs.name: Increment
inputs.description: Defines how quickly / intensively the accumulator counts up

inputs.name: StartValue
inputs.description:
Defines the number with which the accumulator starts counting.

Notice: On-the-fly changes are only applied after the reset trigger has been used

operators.name: BlendValues
operators.description: Blends a number of incoming values with a float value.

operators.name: Damp
operators.description:
Damps (i.e. smoothens or filters) an incoming float value.

See also: [DampVec2], [DampVec3] and [DampFloatList].

inputs.name: Value
inputs.description: Input value to be dampened.

operators.name: DampAngle
operators.description:
Damps (i.e. smoothens or filters) an incoming float value. Avoids flips when jumping from 359 to 0 degrees.

Other damping functions: [Damp], [DampVec2], [DampVec3] and [DampFloatList].

inputs.name: Value
inputs.description: Input value to be dampened.

inputs.name: Damping
inputs.description:
Amount of damping to apply.
The ideal setting for this depends on the range of the input values: Generally, lower damping works better with very large changes in value.

inputs.name: Method
inputs.description:
0: LinearInterpolation. Linear interpolate between the current and target value by the damping amount. Set Damping to 0 for no damping, and to 1 to freeze the current value (and never reach the target).

1: DampedSpring. Uses a "critically damped spring" to provide very smooth interpolation that will never overshoot. For reference, this method is used by Unity's SmoothDamp method.

inputs.name: UseAppRunTime
inputs.description: Advanced setting. Checking this box will cause the damping calculations to use RunTime instead of FxTime for their timing. This means the damping shape/speed will not be affected by any changes you might make to playback speed (such as pausing or reversing the timeline).

operators.name: DetectPulse
operators.description: Detects if rapid changes within an input signal exceed a threshold. This can be useful for detecting beats in OSC or audio signals.

operators.name: Ease
operators.description:
Note: The input value should evolve by steps (e.g., sudden changes) to fully utilize the easing effect.
This operator creates smooth, ease-in-out transitions between changing input values, perfect for animating any step change. Customize the transition style with options like cubic, exponential, or back easing, or choose a linear fallback for a simple interpolation. 
[Damp] [Spring] [EaseVec2] [EaseVec3]

operators.name: EaseKeys
operators.description:
This operator creates smooth, ease-in-out transitions by overriding the easing of keyframes. Customize the transition style with options like cubic, exponential, or back easing, or choose a linear fallback for a simple interpolation. 
Constant interpolation can be achieved by setting the keyframe type to Constant.[EaseVec2Keys] [EaseVec3Keys]

operators.name: FreezeValue
operators.description:
Keeps the current input value as long as Keep is true.
This can be useful for building interactive features like stopwatches.

operators.name: HasValueDecreased
operators.description:
Tests whether the incoming value has decreased by a defined threshold and outputs this as a Boolean

Operator with more Options: [HasValueChanged]

Similar to [HasValueIncreased], [IsGreater] and [HasValueDecreased]

operators.name: Lerp
operators.description: Blends between two values (lerp). Also see [BlendValues] to blend between more values and [Remap] to blend between two value ranges.

operators.name: PeakLevel
operators.description:
Analyzes the incoming value changes and outputs information about the peaks

Output:
1. attack level (float): Attack level
2. foundPeak (bool): Did the incoming value just reach a peak True / False
3. timeSincePeak (float): How much time has passed since the last peak
4. movingSum (float): Passing on the incoming value

operators.name: RemapValues
operators.description: Takes in a list of Vector2 and picks the y component of the pair where X is closest to LookupValue.

operators.name: SmoothStep
operators.description:
Smoothes an incoming animated value

For an alternative with more options see [Damp]

operators.name: Spring
operators.description:
Adds a bounce effect to the incoming value.

Also known as jump, bounce, wobble, rubber, flex

A similar op: [Damp] [SpringVec2] [SpringVec3]

inputs.name: Value
inputs.description: Value Input

inputs.name: Tension
inputs.description:
Defines the rigidity of the spring.
Lower values produce slower and more intense bounce.

inputs.name: Strength
inputs.description:
Defines the strength of the spring.
Higher values produce faster and longer bouncing.

inputs.name: UseAppRunTime
inputs.description:
Checking this box will cause the spring calculations to use RunTime instead of FxTime for their timing.

This means the damping shape/speed will not be affected by any changes you might make to playback speed (such as pausing or reversing the timeline).

operators.name: FloatHash
operators.description: Generates a psydorandom integer from a float value

operators.name: PerlinNoise
operators.description:
Generates a continuously and randomly changing value in the predefined range based on Perlin Noise / Gradient Noise.

Useful to create random looking animations e.g. flickering light, wind, fire, camshake, changing colors etc.

This creates PerlinNoise in 1 dimension. See [PerlinNoise2] and [PerlinNoise3] for Operators with more dimensions

inputs.name: OverrideTime

operators.name: ParticleSystem
operators.description:
Emits particles on emit points and applies the connected forces.

Please check the how-to linked below [HowToUseParticles].

inputs.name: EmitPoints
inputs.description: Input for GPoints

inputs.name: Emit
inputs.description:
Enables emitting of the connected emit points. 

Tip: For simulations of a fixed number of emitted points, you can set the MaxPointCount to -1 and use [Once] or [Trigger] to only trigger an initial emit burst.

inputs.name: Reset
inputs.description:
Clears all emitted points.

Tip: You can connect [HasTimeChanged] to clean up on rewind or looping.

inputs.name: MaxParticleCount
inputs.description:
The length of the cycle buffer holding the simulated particles. Depending on the number of emitted particles it defines the maximum possible particle lifetime.

If set to -1 it will use the count of emit points.

inputs.name: EmitVelocity
inputs.description: An initial velocity that is set for emitted particles along their z-axis.

inputs.name: RadiusFactor
inputs.description:
Some of the forces use the particle radius for collision calculation. The radius is set on emit time by the emit point Scale and this factor.
For consistency we aligned that factor with the default point size for [DrawPoints] which renders points with a radius of 1/100 units.

inputs.name: EmitMode
inputs.description:
This will affect how particles are inserted into the particle buffer. This order will have an effect when drawing with lines.
Note that switching this setting might require resetting the system.

inputs.name: LifeTime
inputs.description:
The lifetime of particles in bars (depending on the current BPM rate).
A negative setting will compute the maximum lifetime from the MaxParticleCount and the number of currently emitted particles.
This will lead to flickering if changing the emit count during playback.

inputs.name: Speed
inputs.description:
The simulation speed. If set to 0 the simulation will be paused.
Negative simulation speed can shortly look like rewinding but the simulation will quickly become inconsistent.

inputs.name: OrientTowardsVelocity
inputs.description: Rotates the particles in relation to their velocity

inputs.name: Drag
inputs.description: A drag factor applied per simulation step. This can be useful for stabilizing simulations where forces insert too much energy (i.e., particle velocity) into the system.

inputs.name: SetF1To
inputs.description:
Can be used for customizing the rendering of the particles.

Note that many operators like [DrawPoints] use the W attribute to control the size of the points.
With other operators like [DrawBillboards] you can use the W parameter to colorize particles over their lifetime.

Keep Original W -> no change
Particle Age -> Normalized age between 0 ... 1
Velocity -> A representation of the particle's velocity.

inputs.name: ParticleForces
inputs.description: Input for Forces or [SwitchParticleForce]

operators.name: AxisStepForce
operators.description:
A force for the [ParticleSystem] that applies random accelerations toward an axis direction. This can lead to interesting results in motion design. If ApplyTrigger is true, a random selection ratio of particles is chosen and accelerated.

Use the following options:

- AxisDistribution to control the frequency of XYZ axis selection.
- AddOriginalVelocity to control whether the original acceleration is replaced or mixed in.
- Set Seed to a value greater than 0 to control randomness. If it's set to 0, the current frame number is used as the random seed.

Please note that the RotationAxis space may depend on the [ParticleSystem.OrientTowardsVelocity] parameter. You can also try combining this effect with [ParticleSystem.Damp] for enhanced results.

operators.name: CollisionForce
operators.description:
A simple simulation of sphere collision between points. The radius of the points is defined on emit by the [ParticleSystem]'s PointRadiusW factor.

Some recommendations:
1. Try to increase the radius (either by increasing the emit points W attribute or the radius factor) and adjust the [DrawPoints] radius accordingly.
2. Try to increase [ParticleSystem] damping.

Slowly align particle velocity with repeated angle steps on the xy-plane. 

It works well when combined with [TurbulenceForce] and [PointTrail].

Note: This will have no effect if the particles have no default velocity or only along the z-axis.

inputs.name: VariationThreshold

A factor that will keep the particle velocity planar to the camera.
This might be useful to emphasize the angled direction if camera rotation changes.

inputs.name: Twist

operators.name: SwitchParticleForce
operators.description:
Switches between connected forces for the ParticleSystem. Can be used to switch between forces or deactivate all.
The index starts with 0 for the first input and will wrap on values exceeding the count of connected inputs.

Tip: 
- use index -1 to activate none (i.e. disable all)
- use index -2 to activate all

Is used with [ParticleSystem] and any force such as [AxisStepForce], [TurbulenceForce] etc.

inputs.name: Index
inputs.description:
Defines which of the incoming Forces is active
-1 disables all forces
-2 activates all forces

operators.name: TextureMapForce
operators.description:
Accelerate particles from a signed normal map. The map is stretched to the camera clip space.

This force can be very powerful in creating effects, such as particles flowing along images or tracing contours. It utilizes the R and G channels of the signed normal map to accelerate along the X and Y axes.

Important: This implies that the normal map needs to have negative values. One option is using [NormalMap] with the Gray_ToNormalizedRGBSigned mode. This can be especially potent when combined with the Rotation parameter.

Tip: You can also use the [ImageLevels] operator to verify that the texture contains negative values.

You can use the ViewConfinement and DepthConcentration parameters to keep the particles within the visible area for the camera view.

Please also check the example.

inputs.name: Amount
inputs.description:
How much are the particles accelerated by the signed normal map.
You can use negative values to invert the direction.

inputs.name: AmountVariation
inputs.description:
Add random variation to the amount of the effect.

Draws points and billboards or quads. This operator is very flexible and allows for a wide spectrum of effects.

Its parameters are grouped into different sections for various aspects of variations.

inputs.name: Scale

inputs.name: Stretch

Non-uniformly scales the billboards

Y = Length

inputs.name: UseWForScale
inputs.description: Defines whether the "W"-attribute of the Points used has an influence on the size of the rendered Billboards

inputs.name: UsePointScale
inputs.description: If enabled, the points' stretch attribute will be applied to the drawn billboards.

inputs.name: Offset
inputs.description: Moves the Billboards' local point space.

inputs.name: Orientation
inputs.description:
Defines how a billboard is aligned towards the camera:

If using point rotation, the orientation to the camera will be ignored.

inputs.name: RotateZ
inputs.description: Rotates a billboard around its own axis without affecting the Orientation.

inputs.name: RotationAxis
inputs.description: Defines how strongly the rotation influences the individual axis.

inputs.name: Randomize
inputs.description: Multiplier for controlling the following random values

inputs.name: RandomPhase
inputs.description:
Phase value for changing the randomness. Can be animated with [Time], for example.
Note that this random seed is continuous and can be used for animations.

inputs.name: RandomPosition
inputs.description: Amount of random offset along X, Y and Z axis.

inputs.name: RandomRotate
inputs.description: Multiplier for random rotation

inputs.name: RandomScale
inputs.description: Multiplier for random uniform scaling

inputs.name: Color
inputs.description:
Defines the color of the Billboards.
If a Texture is used this color will be multiplied.

inputs.name: ColorVariationMode
inputs.description:
Defines how colors from the gradient will be sampled: 

- RandomWithPhase will pick a random color. This will smoothly animate when changing RandomPhase.
- Scatter will pick a random color. Each point gets a random position that will NOT change.
- Spread will use the point's ordering in the buffer. 0 for the first point and 1 for the last. This spreading can be adjusted with the Spread options below.
- W uses the "w" attribute of the points. This can be useful when combined with a [ParticleSystem] that returns particle age in the W attribute.
- FogDistance can be combined with a [SetFog] operator to colorize points depending on their distance to the camera.

inputs.name: ScaleDistribution
inputs.description:
Defines how the scale curve below will be sampled in the range between 0 .. 1. 

- RandomWithPhase will pick a random scale position. This will smoothly animate when changing RandomPhase.
- Scatter will pick a random scale from the curve. Each point gets a random scale that will NOT change.
- Spread will use the point's ordering in the buffer. 0 for the first point and 1 for the last. This spreading can be adjusted with the Spread options below.
- W uses the "w" attribute of the points.
- FogDistance can be combined with a [SetFog] operator to scale points depending on their distance to the camera.

inputs.description: Scaling of the curve. Use the icon in the top right corner to edit this curve in a popup window.

inputs.name: SpreadLength

inputs.name: SpreadPhase
inputs.description: Can offset the spreading range. This can be useful for "sliding" through a gradient of colors or sizes.

inputs.name: SpreadPingPong

operators.name: DrawLines
operators.description:
Draws a point buffer as lines. The lines will be aligned to the camera, but their width will shrink with distance to the camera. You can override this with the ScaleWithDistance parameter. We use the point’s W attribute as a scale factor for the line width. If the W attribute of a point is NaN (Not a Number), that point is not being drawn and acts as a separator between the adjacent line segments. This allows a point buffer to contain multiple disconnected line segments.
DrawLines ignores the orientation defined by the points. Consider using [DrawRibbons] if you need consistent orientation.

Some caveats:
---------------
Long line segments that intersect the camera plane (i.e., one point is in front of the camera and the other behind the camera) will not be rendered correctly. Please consider using [DrawRaypoints] for this.

Performance considerations:
---------------
Drawing lines is fast. Depending on your graphics card, you can draw millions of lines per frame. Performance will be impacted by the length of your lines rather than the point count. This is directly related to your render target’s resolution and multi-sampling level (MSAA).

Defines the color of the Lines.
If a Texture is used this color will be multiplied.

inputs.description: Defines whether Lines cover themselves or are covered by or cover other 3D elements.

inputs.description:
Defines how the texture behaves when repeated.

Wrap: The texture repeats itself continuously
Mirror: The texture is mirrored and repeats infinitely.
Clamp: The texture is cut off at the edge
Border: Unclear
MirrOnce: The texture is mirrored once, then cut off

Renders incoming points as growing strokes. The points' W attribute encodes the U progress of the extension of the strokes.

Another approach would be [SvgToPoints]->[PrepareSvgLineTransition]->[ListToBuffer]->[DrawLinesBuildup].

operators.name: DrawPoints
operators.description:
Draws a point buffer with the set camera, transform, and fog. The points are drawn as camera-facing billboards, ignoring the point orientation. The W attribute of the points is used for scaling. This can be controlled with the UseWForSize parameter.

You can connect a texture to override the round shape.

There are many Operators allowing you to create and manipulate point buffers in countless ways. Please have a look at the examples listed below.

For additional effects, you can experiment with different blend modes or disable depth testing. Note, however, that the points are drawn in the order they are defined in the buffer and not sorted by distance to the camera. This can introduce unwanted artifacts with transparent blending.

Although drawing points is fast, drawing very large points can lead to high fill rates and can drastically impact render performance.

Some notes regarding the size: For historic reasons we apply a 1/10 factor on the size: A point with W=1 will have a radius of 0.01 world units. So a scale of 5 draws a point with a 1 unit diameter.


Also see: [HowToDrawThings], [HowToUsePoints], [DrawLines], [DrawRibbons].
For an Operator with more Options see [DrawBillboards].

There are many Operators allowing you to create and manipulate point buffers in countless ways. Please have a look at the examples listed below.

For additional effects, you can experiment with different blend modes or disable depth testing. Note, however, that the points are drawn in the order they are defined in the buffer and not sorted by distance to the camera. This can introduce unwanted artifacts with transparent blending.

Although drawing points is fast, drawing very large points can lead to high fill rates and can drastically impact render performance.

Also see: [HowToDrawThings], [HowToUsePoints]

We use the points W attribute as a scale factor for the line width.

This helper operator visualizes points and their orientation. It is permanently visible, but you can toggle the default settings for these gizmos using the "Gizmo" toggle in the output window.

Understanding the size, order, and orientation of points in space can be crucial for content creation.

Depending on the use case, this operator can help you visualize:

   The centers
   The "w" attribute (represented by the scale of the center points)
   The "w" attribute (listed as the connected table on the left)
   The orientation with its axes: x (right), y (up), z (forward)
   The orientation as sprites (indicated with an "F")
   The velocity of the points encoded in the rotation (relevant only for Simulation operators).

Also, please take a look at the presets.

It iterates through the source points, excluding those with invalid W values (-nan(ind)), and calculates the minimum and maximum bounds in each dimension (x, y, z). These bounds define the eight points of the bounding box: the minimum and maximum corners of the box. Additionally, it computes the middle point of the bounding box by averaging the minimum and maximum bounds

operators.name: RadialPoints
operators.description:
A versatile generator of circular point sets that can create a variety of circles, spirals, helixes, etc.

Try the presets to get an overview.

Needs a [DrawPoints], [DrawLines] or [DrawMeshAtPoints] or similar in order to become visible.

Similar: [GridPoints], [SpherePoints], [PointsOnMesh]

inputs.name: Count
inputs.description: Amount of points generated between the first and last point

inputs.name: Radius
inputs.description: Radius of radial

inputs.name: OffsetRadius
inputs.description:
This value defines how far the radius of the last point deviates from the radius of the first point.

Especially helpful if Cycles are increased

inputs.name: Center
inputs.description:
Moves the points:

X (-left / +right), 
Y (-down / + up), 
Z (-forward / +backwards)

inputs.name: OffsetCenter
inputs.description:
Moves the position of the last point in relation to the first point:

X (-left / +right), 
Y (-down / + up),
Z (-forward / +backward)

inputs.name: CloseCircleLine
inputs.description:
When drawing the radial points as a closed line, two additional points have to be appended: One at the start position and one as separator.

It will add an overlapping point and a separator, so the number of corners will be Count - 2.

inputs.name: Scale
inputs.description:
The first value will be default uniform scale factor. 
The y component is and offset to that at the end of the point.

inputs.name: F1
inputs.description:
The first value will be default Fx1 value. 
The y component is and offset to that at the end of the point.

inputs.name: F2
inputs.description:
The first value will be default Fx2 value. 
The y component is and offset to that at the end of the point.

operators.name: RepeatAtPoints
operators.description:
Repeats a list of GPU points at positions provided by another list of points. The orientation of the target points can be applied, so this operator can be used to create point instantiation.

If the ApplyTargetScaleW parameter is activated, the W attribute of the target points is used as a scale factor.

Also known as: Copy, Replicate, Instance

Useful combinations: [CommonPointSets] [DrawLines] [DrawPoints]

inputs.name: GTargets
inputs.description: The incoming points define the position at which other points will be distributed

inputs.name: GPoints
inputs.description: Defines what set of points is being distributed

operators.name: RepetitionPoints
operators.description:
Generate a list of points by repeating a transform operation.
This can be very useful in combination with [DrawMeshAtPoints].

Also, by driving the Offset parameter with an LFO, you can produce seamlessly animated endless scenes. This can be useful for VJ projects.

operators.name: SpherePoints
operators.description:
Generates a sphere with evenly distributed points on its surface.

Needs a [DrawPoints], [DrawLines], or [DrawMeshAtPoints] or similar in order to become visible.

Similar: [GridPoints], [RadialPoints], [PointsOnMesh]

inputs.name: Count
inputs.description: Controls the amount of points distributed on the sphere

inputs.name: Radius
inputs.description: Controls the radius of the sphere

inputs.name: Center
inputs.description: Moves the center of the sphere

inputs.name: StartAngle
inputs.description: Rotates the sphere

inputs.name: Scatter
inputs.description:
Shifts the points on the sphere with varying values

ProTip: If the points should leave the surface of the sphere, [RandomizePoints] can be of help

operators.name: SubdivideLinePoints
operators.description: Inserts additional points between line points.

operators.name: _GridPoints_Old
operators.description:
Old version of [GridPoints] with default settings to Bounds. Please use [GridPoints] instead.

Creates a buffer of GPU points distributed on a rectangular or hexagonal grid.

Tips:
- Set any of the counts to 1 to create a plane of points.
- Switch the SizeMode to set if the scaling refers to the padding between the points or the size of the volume.

Needs a [DrawPoints], [DrawLines] or [DrawMeshAtPoints] or similar in order to become visible.

Similar: [RadialPoints], [SpherePoints], [PointsOnMesh]

operators.name: LoadObjAsPoints
operators.description:
Loads an OBJ point cloud file. These files can be generated with Blender or MeshLab and can contain color information.

You can use selected operators like [DrawBillboards] that can use the point rotation attribute (XYZW) as RGBA. This is a hack.

You can also use the [LineVertices] mode to import OBJ files with line definitions and draw them as lines like so:
[LoadObjAsPoints]->[PrepareSvgLineTransition]->[ListToBuffer]->[DrawLinesBuildup]

operators.name: PointToMatrix
operators.description: Converts a point to transform matrix.

operators.name: PointsToCPU
operators.description: Fetches a point list from GPU to CPU. This can be useful for later exporting to a file (e.g., with [ExportPointList]).

operators.name: ReadPointColors
operators.description:
Reads back the `Color` attribute of a structured Point buffer from GPU to CPU as a `List<Vector4>`.

Designed for live LED-strip / WLED output: feeds the `Colors` input of [WLedSerialOutput] without the GPU-pipeline stall that [PointsToCPU] causes in continuous mode.

Default `Async = true` uses a 3-buffer rotation so reads do not block rendering. The data shown is 1-2 frames old, which is invisible for VJ visuals. Set `Async = false` if you need same-frame data and can tolerate the stall.

Reuses one internal `List<Vector4>`, so connecting this op into a per-frame chain is allocation-free after warmup.

AKA: pointcolors, readback, gpu-to-cpu, wled, led-strip, points

operators.name: SampleCpuPoints
operators.description:
Samples a list of line points with cubic bezier spline interpolation. 
This can useful to animate cameras and other objects.

operators.name: _VisualizePointFields
operators.description:
A small helper to visualize the extent of point fields.
Only useful for examples.

operators.name: DataPointImportExport
operators.description: Imports a JSON point list into a GPU structured buffer and optionally exports it again. The node keeps the imported data in an internal buffer, so the points remain visible even when the import trigger is released. It also features an autoload capability that re-imports the file when the ImportFilePath is modified.

inputs.description: An optional incoming point buffer. If a buffer is connected, the Export trigger will use this data. If not connected, Export will use the last successfully imported data.

inputs.description: The path where the JSON file will be saved when Export is triggered.

operators.name: LineTextPoints
operators.description: Loads a single line SVG font and generates a point buffer for a text. This can then be rendered as lines, particle effects, or mesh.

operators.name: LoadSvg
operators.description: Loads an SVG file as points so it can be rendered as points or lines. The supported SVG feature set is very basic, and depending on your exporting applications, elements could be missing or not correctly represented. Missing SVG features include: - Masking - Text - Fill - Effects - Stroke styles like dashes The "ImportAs Lines" mode inserts double points so closed shapes will be closed when rendering lines. To draw the SVG, you can convert the list to a GPU point buffer with [ListToBuffer] and then use [DrawLines]. Also see: [PrepareSvgLineTransition], [SvgLineTransitionExample]

operators.name: PrepareSvgLineTransition
operators.description:
This will iterate over the length of all line segments and compute offsets into W.
DrawLines can then use this offset for animation effects.

0 -

operators.name: AddNoise
operators.description:
Creates a new buffer by resampling the connected points. This can be useful for increasing resolution or smoothing out hard edges.

Also see [SimNoiseOffset] and [TurbulenceForce]

inputs.name: Strength
inputs.description: Defines the total intensity of the random movements.

inputs.name: Frequency
inputs.description: Defines the frequency, i.e., how fast the points move.

inputs.name: Phase
inputs.description: Defines the phase of the noise and can be animated with a [Value], e.g., using [Time].

inputs.name: Variation
inputs.description: Adds more variance and detail to the noise.

inputs.name: AmountDistribution
inputs.description: Multiplier for the individual axes to amplify/attenuate the noise in certain directions.

inputs.name: RotationLookupDistance
inputs.description: Defines the rotation lookup distance

inputs.name: NoiseOffset
inputs.description: Shifts the noise per axis.

operators.name: AttributesFromImageChannels
operators.description: Some test.

operators.name: ClearSomePoints
operators.description: Override a fraction of points with separators to insert gaps into lines.

operators.name: CustomPointShader
operators.description:
A very fast method of writing simple compute shaders to manipulate the connected points.

Each point has the following properties/attributes:

p.Position  // as float3
p.Rotation // as quaternion
p.FX1 // correspond to F1 for scaling and other effects.
p.FX2 // correspond to F2
p.Color // as float4
p.Scale // as float3

The following float values are initialized:

i - index of the point
f - a normalized float value of the index 0 ... 1.

inputs.name: ShaderCode
TimeScale
inputs.description: Warning if this is not enable to 0 the operator will no longer be cached.

operators.name: FilterPoints
operators.description:
Selects (i.e., picks) points based on the given criteria.

Can be used to reduce the overall amount of points to increase performance.

Useful combination [DrawPoints] [MeshFacesPoints] [MeshVerticesToPoints]

Vaguely similar [ClearSomePoints].

inputs.name: Count
inputs.description: Defines how many points are allowed through the filter

inputs.name: StartIndex
inputs.description: Defines which point is defined as the first / starting point

inputs.name: Step
inputs.description:
Defines the distance between the selected points.
Or defines how many points are skipped during the selection if more than two points are passed through the filter.

inputs.name: ScatterSelect
inputs.description: Scatters the selection by adding randomness to the indexes

inputs.name: Seed
inputs.description: Changes the random seed for the scatter effect

operators.name: LinearSamplePointAttributes
operators.description: A variation of [SamplePointAttributes] that uses the point index instead of texture mapping.

operators.name: MapPointAttributes
operators.description:
Sets the points attribute and color from input attributes. This can be very powerful to remap point attributes.

Different modes allow you to...
- distribute the curve range along all points
- or use different mapping ranges.

You can also connect a texture to provide an override for the curve.

inputs.name: InputMode
inputs.description:
Defines how the normalized input value is computed for each point.

- The default will use 0 for the first point and 1 for the last, interpolating between.
- F1 and F2 will use the point attributes. This can be very powerful, e.g., remap the age of particles to a color or size.
- Random will assign a random value between 0 and 1 for each point.

inputs.name: Strength
inputs.description:
Defines how the effect is applied, with 0 effectively bypassing the effect.

Note the values below 0 or above 1 are allowed but might yield unpredictable effects.

inputs.name: Mapping
inputs.description:
Allows the initial input value to be remapped. 
Combining this with Range and Phase can be powerful to build transitions for animated effects.

inputs.name: Range
inputs.description: Can rescale the input range. Smaller value will effectively narrow the range or increase the number of repetitions respectively.

inputs.name: Phase
inputs.description: Allows the range to be shifted. This can be useful to build transitions or cycle through repetitive configurations.

inputs.name: WriteColor
inputs.description: Defines how the gradient colors are applied.

inputs.name: Gradient
inputs.description:
Defines the colors to be applied for remapped input range.

Tip: Try to use a HOLD interpolated gradient with Random input mode.

inputs.name: WriteTo
inputs.description: Defines to which attribute the result should be written.

inputs.name: WriteMode
inputs.description: Allow different configurations of how the new values should be applied.

inputs.name: MappingCurve
inputs.description:
Defines the actual remapping curve. 
Note that only the x-range between 0 and 1 is used.

inputs.name: ValueTexture
inputs.description: Allows overriding the curve with a texture.

operators.name: MoveToSDF
operators.description: Moves points to the nearest SDF surface.

inputs.name: Points
inputs.description: The original points.

inputs.name: Field
inputs.description: The SDF field providing the distance.

inputs.name: Amount
inputs.description:
The factor how much the of the effect is applied.
This can also be negative to move points away from the surface.

inputs.name: MaxSteps
inputs.description:
The maximum number of steps for marching the field.
The max is clamped internally to 100.

inputs.name: MinDistance
inputs.description: The distance at which the raymarching is stopped.

inputs.name: NormalSamplingDistance
inputs.description:
We have to rely on the field's gradient to estimate step direction.
Depending on the provided field, increasing this distance "blurs" the field and thus helps with local inconsistencies.

inputs.name: StepDistanceFactor
inputs.description:
We have to rely on the field's gradient to estimate the marching directions.
This factor is applied on the distance field steps and can help with fields that don't have a constant Lipschitz property.

inputs.name: WriteDistanceMode
inputs.description: Allows to store the distance to the SDF in one of the FX attributes. This might be useful in combinations with [RepeatAtPoints].

inputs.name: SetOrientation
inputs.description:
Apply the SDF normal direction as new point orientation.
This uses an up vector and might be prone to instabilities.

operators.name: PointAttributeFromNoise
operators.description: Changes point attributes with a built-in noise function.

operators.name: PointColorWithField
operators.description: Uses a color field to set point colors from their position in that field.

operators.name: RandomizePoints
operators.description:
Smoothly randomizes various point attributes. It's an extremely versatile operator that provides various options of applying the random modifications and can be smoothly animated.

Note:  This is an updated version of [_RandomizePoints_Legacy1]. It supports phase seeds, colors, extends and different randomization methods and an improved BiasGain method.

inputs.name: Count
inputs.description: The number of resulting points.

inputs.name: SmoothDistance
inputs.description: The smoothing distances for sampling. E.g. 1 rounding over the neighbour points. 2 rounding across two neighbours, etc.

inputs.name: Samples
inputs.description:
The sample count used for smoothing out the result. 
Because higher values can have a significant performance impact, the max count is 10.

inputs.name: Rotation
inputs.description:
Defines how rotation of the interpolated points is computed. 
This rotation can be relevant when resulting points are used for instantiating or repeating other points.

In some situations, the rotation is already inconsistent, e.g. when the position of the points has been randomized without adjusting the rotation. In this case, recomputing the rotation from the line's tangent can be helpful.

inputs.name: RotationUpVector
inputs.description:
When using the "Recompute" rotation mode, this will be used as the up-vector to compute the normal direction of the line.
This basically defines how the line twists around its forward direction.

If the direction of the approaches the up vector, the result becomes unstable because of gimbal lock.

Changes the W value / F value of existing points based on their distance to the active camera.
For example, to make distant points appear larger or smaller than nearby points, etc.
Needs a point source such as: [GridPoints], [RadialPoints], [SpherePoints] etc.
And [DrawPoints], [DrawLines] or similar in order to view the result.

Allows selecting and adding values to points in 3D space via SDF Objects/Fields.
Similar to [SelectPoints].

operators.description: Sets various attributes of points

operators.name: TransformWithImage
operators.description: Allows modifying various point attributes from an image.

operators.name: PointSimulation
operators.description:
Creates a simulation buffer for applying simulation-like force fields, curl noise, or flocking simulation. 

It initially creates a copy of the connected source point buffer. You can then reset to this initial state or constantly blend towards this original state. This can be very helpful to "mix in" a valid state and thus keep a simulation under control.

Although the operators in the namespace lib.point.sim are optimized to apply modifications onto this "simulated" buffer, the [ParticleSystem] provides a more convenient setup for this.

Also see: [SimulateBoidsExample], [HowToUsePoints].

inputs.name: MixOriginal
inputs.description:
Controls how much of the original state is being restored:

- 0: The simulation runs completely free.
- 0.03: A small percentage is constantly mixed into the simulation, thus avoiding too extreme deviations.
- 1: Equivalent to resetting to the source.

For experimental effects, you can use mix values exceeding the range between 0 and 1.

inputs.name: Reset
inputs.description: Completely restores the buffer with the input buffer. This is equivalent to setting MixRate to 1.

inputs.name: Update
inputs.description: Restore input buffer with the MixRate.

inputs.name: MinCapacity
inputs.description:
If the size of the input buffer changes, the simulation will start from scratch.
Setting this optional initial size will only reset the simulation if the new input buffer exceeds the reserved size.

Also see [TurbulenceForce]

operators.name: LegacyParticleSimulation
operators.description:
Note: This operator has been deprecated by [ParticleSystem].

It collects emitted points into a buffer and increases their age over time. The age is stored in the W parameter of the points.

The returned points can be used for particle simulations using operators like...
- [SimNoise], [SimDirectedForce]

... or for drawing with operators like...
- [DrawBillboards], [DrawPoints], [DrawMeshAtPoints]

You can also use the [TrailPoint] operator to create ribbon-like effects.

Note: This was previously called [CollectedSpawnPoints].

operators.name: _LegacySimForwardMovement
operators.description:
Moves points similar to particles into the direction of their Orientation and with W as their current velocity.

With v3.8, the forward movement is done directly in the [ParticleSimulation] operator, which makes this operator obsolete.

operators.name: ApplyRandomWalk
operators.description: Applies random steps to the position and rotation of points.

operators.name: GrowStrains
operators.description:
Uses CollectedSpawnPoints and lines to animate W
as weights moving across the strain with the age of 
the spawn point.

We use a look-up texture that defines the growth 
progression as follows:

- Age from left (birth) to right (death)
- Strain-Length from bottom (root / spawn position) to top.
- R - Width
- G - Noise amount
- B - Twist

operators.name: SimFollowMeshSurface

operators.name: SimPointMeshCollisions

Simulates collisions with meshes.

Note: this is VERY expensive with large meshes (i.e., with more than 100 faces).

operators.name: BoundPoints

Constraints points within a boundary volume
It's the opposite of [BoundingBoxPoints]

operators.description:
Combines points and a mesh and finds the nearest neighbors between points and mesh.
Useful to visualize 'scan effects' and allows the display of complex details.

The example shows the necessary structure.

Needs Points such as [GridPoints], [SpherePoints] etc.
Needs a mesh such as [LoadObj], [TorusMesh] etc.

Becomes visible with [DrawPoints] and [DrawLines] or similar.

operators.name: IkChain

FABRIK inverse kinematic on the GPU. While this operator is still experimental, it works pretty good. Suggestions and help needed.

inputs.name: Influence

inputs.name: PointsPerChain

operators.name: MovePointsToCurveSpace
operators.description:
An advanced op that transforms points into a curved space defined by another set of points.

To understand what this op does, imagine a set of points within a "source space" of a certain extent and orientation. This operator bends the content of that space along a wire defined by a set of target points.
After that, the source axis will be located on the line.

This op requires a careful setup of the orientation of target points! Use [VisualizePoints] to make sure that the target points face with the z-axis along the line (i.e., "forward" or "tangential").
You can use the [ResampleLinePoints] operator to recompute the orientation.

Similar to [MoveMeshToLinePoints]

inputs.name: SourcePoints
inputs.description: The points that will be transformed.

inputs.name: TargetPoints
inputs.description: A point set that defines the target curve. These points MUST be oriented with their Z-axis along the line!

inputs.name: Extent
inputs.description:
The extent of the source volume. Increasing the extent will shrink the resulting geometry.
Enable gizmo visualization to see it.

inputs.name: Pivot
inputs.description: An optional offset on the source space.

inputs.name: SourceAlignment
inputs.description: The axis that will become the center of the curve.

inputs.name: Range
inputs.description: The range of the curve that will be used for mapping.

inputs.name: Offset
inputs.description: Slides the points along the curve. This is similar to adjusting the corresponding axis of the Pivot parameter.

inputs.name: Scale
inputs.description: Scale of the resulting space.

inputs.name: AtBoundaries

operators.name: PointLight
operators.description:
The standard point light with transform gizmo.
This can bring light into your scene using a combination of "Color", "Intensity" and "Decay".
Beware that [SetEnvironment] also affects the lighting in your scene, even if you are not using it, because every scene is always lit by a Default CubeMap (that can be deactivated by manually adding a [SetEnvironment]).

Currently a maximum of 8 Pointlights can be used in your scene. For example by daisychaining them right before your graph goes into the camera.

inputs.name: Position
inputs.description:
Changes the position of the PointLight:

X (-left / +right), 
Y (-down / +up), 
Z (-forward / +backwards)

inputs.name: Intensity
inputs.description: Increases or decreases the intensity of the light in relation to its decay.

inputs.name: Color
inputs.description: Sets the color of the light.

inputs.name: IsEnabled
inputs.description: Turns the PointLight On / Off

inputs.name: Decay
inputs.description:
Controls how far the light shines into the scene.

A low decay setting means the light is shining far.
A high decay setting means the light reaches a short distance.

operators.name: SetEnvironment
operators.description:
Sets the image-based lighting (IBL) for the current RenderTarget. This texture can then be used by drawing operators for physically based rendering (PBR) further left in the graph.
The operators needed are: [LoadImage] -> [TextureToCubeMap] -> [SetEnvironment]


Some background information: a standard technology for rendering is to use environment textures that store various degrees of roughness in their mip map levels: fully reflective chrome in the highest resolution and very blurry/diffuse reflections in the lower levels. This is not just done by blurring, though: a single ultra bright pixel (e.g. the sun) can brighten the complete diffuse reflection. This computation is very(!) expensive and should not be done in real-time for high resolution environment maps.

To compute this IBL map [SetEnvironment] needs a cube map texture. As of now you can load equirectangular HDR maps only in DDS format and convert them with a [TextureToCubemap]. We are working on making this more convenient. You can also use procedural image textures for this.

NOTICE: For the background environment to have the correct alignment, the camera must be set after the environment:

[DrawMesh]->[SetMaterial]->[SetPointLight]->[SetEnvironment]->[SetCamera].

Also see: [HowToDrawThings]

inputs.name: Texture
inputs.description:
Cubemap input to overwrite the default cubemap.
This can be used with the [TextureToCubeMap] operator.

inputs.name: UpdateLive
inputs.description:
Refreshes any changes to the image and exposure settings. This can be kept turned on but will significantly decrease rendering performance.

If turned on this allows animated "Exposure" values and live changes in the incoming image.

inputs.name: Exposure
inputs.description:
Defines the intensity with which the scene is illuminated by the image.

If changing this value has no effect temporarily turn on and off the "UpdateLive" setting.

inputs.name: RenderBackground
inputs.description: If turned on the environment will be visible to the camera by being mapped on a sphere mesh around the scene.

inputs.name: BackgroundBlur
inputs.description: Defines how much the image on the sphere in the background is blurred.

inputs.name: BackgroundColor
inputs.description:
Tints the background with the selected color.

Does not affect the color of the light and/or reflection.

inputs.name: BackgroundDistance
inputs.description:
Sets the radius for the sphere mesh that surrounds the scene.

ProTip: Clipping of the background can be prevented either by this setting or by the "NearFarClip" settings in the used camera.

inputs.name: QualityFactor
inputs.description:
A factor that is applied to the sample count for the different roughness levels.
When enabling Live update this has significant(!) impact on your rendering performance, so turn this down until the artifacts are noticable.

operators.name: SetFog
operators.description:
Adds fog to the incoming scene.

ProTip: If large meshes (for example a "quadmesh" as a ground plane) are not properly obscured by the fog, one possible reason could be that the tessellation is not high enough.

Useful combinations [ColorGradeDepth]. An operator that allows objects far away from the camera to be colored differently than close objects.

Also see [SetEnvironment] and [DepthBufferAsGrayScale]

operators.name: SetMaterial
operators.description:
Sets the Physically Based Rendering (PBR) Material for the current RenderTarget which is then used by [DrawMesh] and other PBR rendering operators. Each of the material properties can be controlled by a color and/or by connecting a texture input by using a [LoadImage] operator.

Please note that the color parameter is multiplied to the texture: so for an emissive texture to be visible, you have to first set the Emissive Color to white (or 1,1,1).

The base (albedo) color can also be adjusted by the Draw operators.
Please use [CombineMaterialChannels] to combine Roughness, Metallic and Occlusion textures into a single texture that can be connected to the .RoughnessMetallicOcclusion parameter.
For the roughness rendering the draw operators need an IBL texture set by [SetEnvironment]. If [SetEnvironment] is not used there is still a predefined default IBL.


Also see: [HowToDrawThings]

If no normalmap is available [NormalMap] can be used to generate one.

operators.name: SetPointLight
operators.description:
Adds a point light into the scene which illuminates geometry using a combination of "Color", "Intensity" and "Decay".

Beware that [SetEnvironment] also affects the lighting in your scene, even if you are not using it, because every scene is always lit by a Default CubeMap (that can be deactivated by manually adding a [SetEnvironment]).

Currently a maximum of 8 Pointlights can be used in your scene. For example by daisy-chaining them right before your graph goes into the camera.

If changing values and settings in this Operator does not cause any changes in the Viewport, it may be necessary to (temporarily) activate 'UpdateLive' in the following [SetEnvironment] op.

Creates Points and Sprites from text that can be animated and then rendered with [DrawPointSprites] or [DrawPointSpritesShaded].
